source_passages.quotation: 4. **Capacity, the last step of Evening after drawing and discarding:** Satchel **plus Damaged box** may contain **six items plus two per face-up bag on its track**. Track items do not count toward load. Permanently remove chosen Satchel/Damaged items until within limit. Do not check capacity immediately upon acquiring an item.

answer.part: How is Vagabond capacity calculated, what counts toward load, when is it checked and where do excess items go?
answer.ruling: Capacity is six items plus two per face-up bag on its track. Count Satchel plus Damaged box; track items do not count. Check at last step of Evening after drawing and discarding; permanently remove chosen Satchel/Damaged items until within limit. Do not check immediately on acquiring an item.

source_passages.quotation: 1. **Refresh:** First count tea **already face up on Refresh track**; flip two exhausted items face up per counted tea, then three more exhausted items. Tea refreshed during this step gives no extra refresh this step. Refreshing changes face, not damaged status.
- **Repair:** Exhaust hammer; move one damaged item to Satchel **keeping current face**. Ready tea/coins/bags move to tracks if space.
1. If in forest, **Rest**: return all damaged items to Satchel and flip them face up; ready tea/coins/bags move to tracks if able. This does not refresh undamaged exhausted items.

answer.part: Does forest Rest refresh an undamaged exhausted item, and how does it differ from Refresh or Repair?
answer.ruling: Forest Rest returns all damaged items to Satchel and flips them face up; it does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. Refresh flips exhausted items according to face-up tea already on Refresh track, then three more. Repair exhausts hammer and moves one damaged item to Satchel keeping its face.

source_passages.quotation: - **Aid:** Exhaust **one face-up, undamaged item of any type**, give a card matching your clearing to player with faction pieces there, even Hostile. May then take one item from their Crafted Items box face up into Satchel/track; no available item is required to Aid. **Only non-Hostile relationships can advance through Aid; a Hostile recipient stays Hostile.** Check relationship improvement below.

**Relationships:** Each other faction starts Indifferent. To advance a non-Hostile marker one space, Aid that faction as many times **in this same turn** as printed between current and next spaces. One Aid counts toward only one improvement. Advance and score VP printed in new space. At final space become **Allied**; each subsequent Aid to that faction scores **two VP**.
- Aid cannot move marker out of Hostile; it can still obtain a crafted item. Coalition with Hostile faction resets its marker to Indifferent.

answer.part: What is Vagabond Aid cost and target, is a crafted item required, and how are repeated Aid relationship improvements counted?
answer.ruling: Aid exhausts one face-up undamaged item of any type and gives a card matching current clearing to a player with faction pieces there, even if Hostile. It may then take one item from that player’s Crafted Items, but no item is required. To advance a non-Hostile relationship one space, Aid that faction as many times in the same turn as printed between current and next spaces; each Aid counts toward only one improvement. At Allied, subsequent Aid scores 2 VP. Aid cannot reduce Hostile.

source_passages.quotation:
- **Aid:** Each subsequent Aid to this Allied faction scores **two VP**.
- **Move:** May force warriors of **one** Allied faction to accompany the pawn to its destination clearing. They follow their own movement restrictions, including rule and Eyrie tie advantage. They cannot accompany a move specified to be alone. Moving them into sympathy triggers Outrage.
- **Attack with an increased hit limit:** At the start of battle **as attacker**, you may treat warriors of **one** Allied faction in the battle clearing as your own. **Add those warriors to all your undamaged swords to determine your maximum rolled hits**. They can join against a different enemy; you cannot use an ally's warriors to attack that ally itself.

answer.part: What changes at Allied status: Aid points, moving warriors and attacking with them, and can you use allied warriors against their own faction?
answer.ruling: At Allied, subsequent Aid scores 2 VP. Vagabond may force warriors of one Allied faction to accompany a move, obeying their own move restrictions; moving them into sympathy triggers Outrage, and they cannot accompany a move specified to be alone. At battle start as attacker, it may treat one Allied faction’s warriors in clearing as its own and add them to all undamaged swords for maximum rolled hits. It cannot use them to attack that ally.

source_passages.quotation: **Taking hits with an ally:** In a battle using Allied warriors as your own, you may absorb hits by removing those warriors or damaging your items. If you remove **more allied warriors than items you damage in that battle**, the ally becomes Hostile **at battle end**. This overrides ordinary hostility timing for those friendly warriors taken as hits against the other enemy. Equal numbers do not trigger the rule.

answer.part: When Vagabond takes hits using allied warriors, when and under what comparison does that ally become Hostile?
answer.ruling: In battle using Allied warriors as your own, Vagabond may absorb hits by removing allied warriors or damaging items. If it removes more allied warriors than items damaged in that battle, the ally becomes Hostile at battle end. Equal numbers do not trigger it.

source_passages.quotation: - **Vagabond cost and reuse:** The pawn **may activate repeatedly in a turn**. For each icon, **pay by exhausting one face-up, undamaged hammer: flip that hammer face down**. The pawn's **current clearing must match every icon on the card**. Reusing the pawn never waives the hammer payment per icon. One clearing cannot pay mixed fox/rabbit/mouse icons.

- **Craft:** Exhaust one hammer per crafting icon; pawn acts as crafting piece matching current clearing, and may activate repeatedly despite normal once-per-turn crafting limit. Clearing must match **all icons**; cannot craft mixed fox/rabbit/mouse requirements from one clearing. When you craft an item, you may immediately take that item face up into Satchel/track and **use it for another Daylight action immediately**, if its cost and other requirements are met. Need supply item as usual.

answer.part: Can Vagabond craft a card requiring fox and rabbit icons from one clearing, reuse the pawn for multiple craftings, and immediately use a crafted item?
answer.ruling: Vagabond’s pawn may activate repeatedly, but its current clearing must match every crafting icon; one clearing cannot pay mixed fox/rabbit/mouse requirements. It pays one face-up undamaged hammer per icon. When crafting an item, it may immediately take it face up into Satchel/track and use it for another Daylight action immediately if cost and other requirements are met.

source_passages.quotation:
| Thief | boot, torch, tea, sword | **Steal:** exhaust torch to take random hand card from player with faction pieces in your clearing |
| Tinker | boot, torch, bag, hammer | **Day Labor:** exhaust torch to take discard-pile card matching clearing; bird always qualifies |
| Ranger | boot, torch, crossbow, sword | **Hideout:** exhaust torch to repair three items, keeping their faces; immediately end Daylight and begin Evening |

answer.part: List base Vagabond characters with starting items and special action costs/results, including Ranger timing.
answer.ruling: Thief starts boot, torch, tea, sword; Steal exhausts torch to take a random hand card from player with faction pieces in clearing. Tinker starts boot, torch, bag, hammer; Day Labor exhausts torch to take discard-pile card matching clearing, bird always qualifies. Ranger starts boot, torch, crossbow, sword; Hideout exhausts torch to repair three items keeping their faces, immediately ends Daylight and begins Evening.

source_passages.quotation: - **Explore:** Exhaust torch in ruin's clearing. Take one hidden item face up into Satchel or track; score one VP if an item taken. Remove ruin when its last item is taken, freeing the building slot.

Clearings have fox, rabbit or mouse suit and limited building slots. Buildings require open slots; tokens do not occupy these. Ruins block their slots and can be removed only when explicitly allowed. A forest is enclosed by printed paths and clearings; it is adjacent to clearings touching it without crossing a printed path and to forests separated by just one printed path. Winter's river also divides forests. (2.2–2.4, M.1–2.)

answer.part: After removing a ruin last item, what happens to its building slot, and can ordinary building placement remove a ruin instead?
answer.ruling: When the last item is taken from a ruin, remove the ruin and free the building slot. Ruins can be removed only when explicitly allowed; ordinary building placement does not remove them.

source_passages.quotation: **Vagabond coalition (9.2.8):** Cannot activate normal dominance win. With **four or more players**, during own Daylight at **at least 10 VP**, activate dominance to coalition with another player **not already in coalition**, whose VP is lowest among players other than you (choose among ties). Put your score marker on partner's faction board and stop scoring. If partner wins, you also win, including if partner wins through dominance. Coalition partners are not enemies. A Hostile partner becomes Indifferent. Coalition does not by itself grant Allied relationship powers.

answer.part: Can a coalition partner be attacked as an enemy, and does coalition automatically grant Allied relationship powers?
answer.ruling: Coalition partners are not enemies. Coalition alone does not grant Allied relationship powers.

source_passages.quotation: - **Hostile:** Removing **one** warrior of a non-Hostile faction immediately moves marker to Hostile (except allied battle-loss rule above). **Infamy:** During battle on your own turn, score **one extra VP per hostile piece removed**, except warrior that first made faction Hostile. **Each hostile building/token removed in battle on your turn normally scores two VP: one removal VP plus one Infamy. A hostile warrior scores one Infamy, except the warrior that first caused Hostile status.** Infamy depends on whose turn it is, rather than which side attacks: no Infamy on another player's turn, and none from Strike. Hostile status requires extra boot for moves into hostile warriors, not merely buildings/tokens.

**30 VP:** First to 30 wins immediately, on any player's turn. If multiple reach 30 simultaneously, tied player closest clockwise to current player wins, including current player. Removing enemy buildings/tokens gives one VP each regardless of phase or whether attacker/defender. Crafting items scores printed VP except Eyrie's Disdain. Faction scoring is described above. (3.1–2.)

Faction/card scoring can add to these ordinary points. In particular, Vagabond Infamy is an **additional** point per eligible Hostile piece in battle on his own turn, except the warrior that first caused Hostile status. Do not add an ordinary removal point for a warrior.

answer.part: A Vagabond battles a previously non-Hostile faction on its own turn, removes two warriors followed by one building. How much removal/Infamy VP, and why?
answer.ruling: On Vagabond’s own battle turn, two warriors removed from a non-Hostile faction yield no ordinary removal VP; the first warrior makes that faction Hostile and is excluded from Infamy, while the second hostile warrior yields 1 Infamy VP. The building yields 1 ordinary removal VP plus 1 Infamy VP, total 2. Total for described pieces: 3 VP.

source_passages.quotation: - **Move:** Exhaust one boot, plus **one extra boot** if destination has any warriors of any Hostile faction (also for forced moves). Ignore rule. **Cannot enter a forest with this action; from a forest you may move only to an adjacent clearing.** Slip has the special free-boot exception.

- **Hostile:** Removing **one** warrior of a non-Hostile faction immediately moves marker to Hostile (except allied battle-loss rule above). **Infamy:** During battle on your own turn, score **one extra VP per hostile piece removed**, except warrior that first made faction Hostile. **Each hostile building/token removed in battle on your turn normally scores two VP: one removal VP plus one Infamy. A hostile warrior scores one Infamy, except the warrior that first caused Hostile status.** Infamy depends on whose turn it is, rather than which side attacks: no Infamy on another player's turn, and none from Strike. Hostile status requires extra boot for moves into hostile warriors, not merely buildings/tokens.

answer.part: What is the cost of a normal Vagabond move into a clearing with only hostile buildings versus one with hostile warriors from several factions?
answer.ruling: A normal move into hostile buildings/tokens only costs one boot; Hostile status requires extra boot only when destination has hostile warriors, regardless of how many hostile factions’ warriors are there. Thus hostile warriors from several factions still add one extra boot total.

source_passages.quotation: **Dominance (3.3):** In own Daylight at **at least 10 VP**, activate a dominance card from hand into play area; remove score marker and stop scoring VP. Cannot remove/replace activated card. At **start of own Birdsong**, win if ruling **three clearings of matching mouse/rabbit/fox suit**, or for **bird dominance, two diagonally opposite corner clearings**. Meeting condition earlier does not immediately win. Dominance cards cannot be crafted, but can be spent for suit. Whenever one would enter discard, put it near map available instead. During own Daylight, spend matching card to take available dominance into hand. Available **bird dominance remains bird**, so payment must be bird; a bird hand card can pay for non-bird dominance. Activation and taking are separate, neither requires a faction action allowance.

answer.part: Does taking an available dominance card activate it immediately, and do taking/activating use a Marquise action?
answer.ruling: Taking an available dominance card puts it in hand; activation is a separate action in own Daylight at 10+ VP. Taking and activation are not faction actions and neither uses Marquise action allowance.

source_passages.quotation: The base game has a Fall/Winter board, two battle dice, four faction boards, 54 shared-deck cards, 16 faction overviews, 4 Eyrie leaders and 2 Loyal Viziers, 3 Vagabond characters and 15 quests. There are 25 Marquise, 20 Eyrie and 10 Alliance warriors; one Vagabond pawn; 7 roosts, 6 each of sawmills, workshops and recruiters, 3 bases; 10 sympathy, 8 wood and 1 keep token; 4 ruins, 4 score markers, 3 relationship markers, 12 clearing markers and 23 items. Items are boots, swords, bags, hammers, tea, coins, crossbows and a torch. Items are not faction pieces or enemy pieces. **Faction-piece ownership cannot change**: each player owns the faction chosen in setup and its listed faction pieces, except items; possessing an item does not make it faction-owned.

answer.part: Can ownership of faction pieces change, and are items faction pieces that belong to the faction holding them?
answer.ruling: Faction-piece ownership cannot change: each player owns the faction selected in setup and its listed faction pieces, except items. Possessing an item does not make it faction-owned; items are not faction or enemy pieces.

source_passages.quotation: - Immediate effect (paper box): resolve, then discard the **crafting card**. An item card requires the corresponding **item token** in the map supply, or it cannot be crafted. Take the item token into Crafted Items and score the VP printed on the card, subject to Eyrie exception. The item token stays; the crafting card is discarded. Ordinary factions do not exhaust crafted items as Vagabond does.

| Immediate-effect crafting card | Your hand | Shared discard pile after resolving |
| Persistent-effect crafting card | Your hand | Your play area |
| Item token produced by an item card | Map item supply | Crafting faction’s Crafted Items box; when Vagabond itself crafts, it may immediately take its crafted item face up into Satchel/track |

- Persistent effect (stone box): keep card in your play area and gain its text, subject to the personal duplicate check above. Its card is outside your hand and cannot be spent/discarded/used for another purpose unless explicitly instructed.

answer.part: What happens to immediate-effect versus persistent crafting cards, and can a card in your play area be spent as though in hand?
answer.ruling: Immediate-effect crafting card resolves then is discarded to shared discard. Persistent-effect card stays in play area, outside hand, and cannot be spent/discarded/used for another purpose unless explicitly instructed. Crafted item token goes from map supply to Crafted Items box (or Vagabond may take its own craft immediately).

source_passages.quotation: - **Ambush cards cannot be crafted:** the defender may play one for two immediate hits, or the attacker may play one to foil a defending ambush, matching the clearing. **Dominance cards cannot be crafted:** activate one to change victory condition, or spend it for suit.

answer.part: Can ambush or dominance cards be crafted, and what are their other permitted uses?
answer.ruling: Ambush cards cannot be crafted: defender may play one for two immediate hits, or attacker may play one to foil defending ambush, matching clearing. Dominance cards cannot be crafted: activate to change victory condition or spend for suit.

source_passages.quotation:
1. Choose factions; determine starting player and seating randomly. Take faction boards and their listed pieces. Use Fall or Winter. Fall has no special rules; on Winter, the river divides forests just as printed paths do. Rivers are otherwise not paths.
2. Put score markers at 0.
3. With two players, remove all four dominance cards. Shuffle shared deck; each player draws **three cards**.
4. **Ruins and items:** Cover the four R building slots with ruins. The separate map item supply is **2 boots, 2 bags, 1 crossbow, 1 hammer, 2 swords, 2 tea, 2 coins**. Keep the four R-marked ruin items separate from this supply: only Vagabond faction setup hides one each of its R-marked bag, boot, hammer and sword beneath the four ruins, **one item beneath each ruin**. During that Vagabond setup, shuffle the ruin/item stacks and return each to an empty R ruin slot, keeping item identities hidden. Without a Vagabond, ruins contain no items.
5. The map item supply uses its corresponding spaces near the top of the map.
6. Distribute overview cards as desired; put battle dice nearby.
7. Set up factions in their letter order: Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond. Setup order is distinct from turn order.

answer.part: In standard setup how are starting player/seating, score markers and dice arranged, and does faction setup order set turn order?
answer.ruling: Standard setup randomly determines starting player and seating; take faction boards and listed pieces, choose Fall or Winter, put score markers at 0. Two-player setup removes four dominance cards and each draws three after shuffling shared deck. Faction setup sequence is Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond; it is distinct from turn order. Battle dice are placed nearby.

source_passages.quotation: **30 VP:** First to 30 wins immediately, on any player's turn. If multiple reach 30 simultaneously, tied player closest clockwise to current player wins, including current player. Removing enemy buildings/tokens gives one VP each regardless of phase or whether attacker/defender. Crafting items scores printed VP except Eyrie's Disdain. Faction scoring is described above. (3.1–2.)

answer.part: When does the ordinary 30-VP victory take effect: must the player finish the action, phase, or turn first?
answer.ruling: First to 30 VP wins immediately, on any player’s turn. No need to finish action, phase, or turn.

source_passages.quotation: **Battle (4.3):** Choose a clearing with your warriors or pawn and an enemy there as defender. **Battle does not require you to rule the clearing.** Resolve these six steps:

answer.part: What pieces must you have in the clearing to initiate an ordinary battle, whom can you choose as defender, and must you rule that clearing?
answer.ruling: Choose a clearing with your warriors or pawn and an enemy there as defender. Battle does not require you to rule the clearing.

source_passages.quotation: 2. **Before-roll effects:** Resolve applicable effects; attacker chooses order if both have them.
4. **After-roll effects:** Resolve effects affecting battle that do not say “before rolling”; attacker chooses order if both have them.

6. **Deal hits:** Each hit removes one opposing piece. The side taking hits chooses its own removal order, but **all its warriors must be removed before its buildings/tokens**. It also chooses order of effects triggered by its pieces' removal. Both sides deal their counted hits; losing warriors does not retroactively change the rolled cap. Whoever removes an enemy building/token scores **one VP each**, even while defending and even outside battle. Vagabond takes hits as item damage instead.

answer.part: Who orders both players' before-roll and after-roll battle effects, and who orders effects triggered by a side's pieces being removed?
answer.ruling: For before-roll and after-roll battle effects, attacker chooses the order if both sides have applicable effects. The side taking hits chooses order of effects triggered by its own pieces’ removal.

source_passages.quotation: 5. **Count hits:** Add extra hits (uncapped by warriors), subtract ignored hits. If defender has no warriors, attacker deals one extra hit for **defenseless**; Vagabond is instead defenseless if it has no undamaged swords.

answer.part: In the Count Hits step, how do effects that ignore hits change the total?
answer.ruling: In Count Hits, add extra hits (not capped by warriors), then subtract ignored hits.

source_passages.quotation: - Immediate effect (paper box): resolve, then discard the **crafting card**. An item card requires the corresponding **item token** in the map supply, or it cannot be crafted. Take the item token into Crafted Items and score the VP printed on the card, subject to Eyrie exception. The item token stays; the crafting card is discarded. Ordinary factions do not exhaust crafted items as Vagabond does.

**Lords of the Forest:** Win ties for rule if at least one Eyrie piece there. **Disdain for Trade:** Crafted items score only **one VP instead of printed VP** (other extra crafting-point effects still apply). Builder ignores Disdain.

answer.part: When a non-Vagabond base faction crafts an item, where does that item come from and where is it placed, and what is the usual VP reward?
answer.ruling: An item card requires the corresponding item token in map supply or cannot be crafted. Take token from map supply into crafting faction’s Crafted Items box and score the VP printed on card, except Eyrie Disdain (one VP); the crafting card itself is discarded for an immediate effect or kept for persistent effect.

source_passages.quotation:
- **Marquise, Eyrie and Alliance cost:** For **each icon**, activate **one workshop, roost or sympathy in a clearing matching that icon's suit**, respectively. A crafting piece gets its suit from its clearing. Combine eligible pieces as needed, but **each piece may activate only once per turn**.
- **Vagabond cost and reuse:** The pawn **may activate repeatedly in a turn**. For each icon, **pay by exhausting one face-up, undamaged hammer: flip that hammer face down**. The pawn's **current clearing must match every icon on the card**. Reusing the pawn never waives the hammer payment per icon. One clearing cannot pay mixed fox/rabbit/mouse icons.
- A **three-color question-mark icon** accepts any suit.

answer.part: Which crafting pieces do the Eyrie and Alliance activate, how is a crafting piece's suit determined, and what does a three-color question-mark crafting icon require?
answer.ruling: Eyrie activates roosts and Alliance activates sympathy, one matching piece per icon. Each piece’s suit comes from the clearing containing it. A three-color question-mark icon accepts any suit.

source_passages.quotation:
- **Craft** from hand with sympathy.
- **Mobilize:** Add one hand card to Supporters. With no base on map, keep at most five supporters and discard incoming overflow; with any base, the stack has no cap.
- **Train during Daylight:** Spend a **hand card** matching a clearing with a base to place one supply warrior in Officers box. Supporters cannot pay Train. Each officer allows one Evening military operation; taking operations does not consume officers.

answer.part: How does Alliance Mobilize work, and must Alliance finish all crafting before mobilizing or training during Daylight?
answer.ruling: Mobilize adds one hand card to Supporters. With no base, keep at most five and discard incoming overflow; with any base, no cap. Alliance may craft, Mobilize, and Train in any order and number during Daylight.

source_passages.quotation: **Evening, even after turmoil:** Score the VP on rightmost empty roost-track space. Draw one plus uncovered draw bonuses; discard down to five.

answer.part: How does the Eyrie score and draw in an ordinary Evening, and does the scoring still happen after Turmoil?
answer.ruling: Each Evening score VP on rightmost empty roost-track space, draw one plus uncovered draw bonuses, and discard down to five. The same normal Evening occurs after Turmoil.

source_passages.quotation: **Pawn and items:** Pawn is not a warrior, cannot rule or block rule, and cannot be removed. An enemy effect removing **all enemy pieces** from its clearing instead damages **three items**. Items may be face up (ready) or face down (exhausted), and independently undamaged or damaged. To exhaust for an action, choose a face-up **undamaged** item and flip it down. Damaged items cannot pay actions.

- **Battle:** Exhaust one sword to initiate. Maximum rolled hits, attacking or defending, equals **all undamaged swords in Satchel, face up or face down**. As defender you are defenseless only with no undamaged swords. Take hits as item damage.

answer.part: What does the Vagabond pay to initiate its Daylight Battle action, and can an exhausted undamaged sword pay that cost merely because it still counts for rolled hits?
answer.ruling: Vagabond Battle exhausts one sword to initiate. An exhausted sword cannot pay because actions require a face-up undamaged item, although all undamaged swords in Satchel face up or down count toward rolled-hit maximum.

source_passages.quotation: Take turns clockwise: **Birdsong → Daylight → Evening**. “At start” effects precede all other phase effects; “at end” effects follow everything else in that phase, before next phase. Once the last step of a turn begins, no other actions are allowed except explicitly end-of-Evening/turn actions. An action, ability or persistent effect cannot be interrupted unless an effect explicitly permits it; a Marquise March's two moves are one compound action. If simultaneous effects have no clear order or decision maker, the player taking the turn chooses. For battle effects at the same timing, attacker chooses their order. (1.1.3, 1.4, 4.3.)

answer.part: What is the order of phases in a turn, and whose turn begins after Evening ends?
answer.ruling: Turns proceed clockwise through Birdsong → Daylight → Evening. After Evening the next player clockwise takes a turn.

source_passages.quotation: Face-up tea/coins/bags in Satchel immediately move to empty matching track space if possible; each track holds at most three of its type. Exhausting an item on track sends it to Satchel. Boots/swords/crossbows/torch/hammers are gained face up in Satchel. Damaging an item sends it to Damaged box **without changing its face**. One hit damages one undamaged item of your choice; ignore excess hits when none remain.

answer.part: When Vagabond takes a hit, which item must be chosen, where does it go, does its face change, and can already-damaged items absorb another hit?
answer.ruling: Each hit damages one undamaged item of Vagabond’s choice; it goes to Damaged box without changing its face. Already damaged items cannot absorb another hit; excess hits are ignored if no undamaged items remain.

source_passages.quotation: **Evening:** The four military operations are **Move, Battle, Recruit and Organize**. Take **up to your number of officers** in operations, in any order and repetition. Officers stay on the board; taking an operation does not consume an officer. After operations, draw one card plus one per uncovered draw bonus, then discard hand down to five.
| Recruit | Place one warrior at one clearing with a base |

answer.part: During Alliance Evening, how many military operations may be taken, and for one Recruit operation how many warriors are placed and where?
answer.ruling: Alliance takes up to its number of officers in Evening operations, in any order and repetition; one Recruit operation places one warrior at one clearing with a base.

source_passages.quotation:
**Daylight:** Any order/number, as ready undamaged items permit:

- **Move:** Exhaust one boot, plus **one extra boot** if destination has any warriors of any Hostile faction (also for forced moves). Ignore rule. **Cannot enter a forest with this action; from a forest you may move only to an adjacent clearing.** Slip has the special free-boot exception.
- **Battle:** Exhaust one sword to initiate. Maximum rolled hits, attacking or defending, equals **all undamaged swords in Satchel, face up or face down**. As defender you are defenseless only with no undamaged swords. Take hits as item damage.
- **Explore:** Exhaust torch in ruin's clearing. Take one hidden item face up into Satchel or track; score one VP if an item taken. Remove ruin when its last item is taken, freeing the building slot.
- **Aid:** Exhaust **one face-up, undamaged item of any type**, give a card matching your clearing to player with faction pieces there, even Hostile. May then take one item from their Crafted Items box face up into Satchel/track; no available item is required to Aid. **Only non-Hostile relationships can advance through Aid; a Hostile recipient stays Hostile.** Check relationship improvement below.
- **Quest (matching clearing only):** Choose a face-up quest matching clearing; exhaust its **two listed items**, put quest in play area completed. Choose either VP equal to matching completed quests **including this one**, or draw two cards. Draw replacement quest into public display. No cards are spent to pay a quest.
- **Strike:** Exhaust crossbow to remove one enemy warrior in clearing. Only if that enemy has no warriors there may you remove another of its faction pieces instead. Check hostility. Strike is not battle and gives no Infamy.
- **Repair:** Exhaust hammer; move one damaged item to Satchel **keeping current face**. Ready tea/coins/bags move to tracks if space.
- **Craft:** Exhaust one hammer per crafting icon; pawn acts as crafting piece matching current clearing, and may activate repeatedly despite normal once-per-turn crafting limit. Clearing must match **all icons**; cannot craft mixed fox/rabbit/mouse requirements from one clearing. When you craft an item, you may immediately take that item face up into Satchel/track and **use it for another Daylight action immediately**, if its cost and other requirements are met. Need supply item as usual.
- **Special:** Exhaust items required by character action below.

answer.part: How many Daylight actions may the Vagabond take, must the action types follow a fixed order, and may the same action type be repeated?
answer.ruling: Vagabond Daylight allows any order and number of actions as ready undamaged items permit; action types have no fixed order and may be repeated.

source_passages.quotation: **Pawn and items:** Pawn is not a warrior, cannot rule or block rule, and cannot be removed. An enemy effect removing **all enemy pieces** from its clearing instead damages **three items**. Items may be face up (ready) or face down (exhausted), and independently undamaged or damaged. To exhaust for an action, choose a face-up **undamaged** item and flip it down. Damaged items cannot pay actions.

- **Strike:** Exhaust crossbow to remove one enemy warrior in clearing. Only if that enemy has no warriors there may you remove another of its faction pieces instead. Check hostility. Strike is not battle and gives no Infamy.

answer.part: What item and how many of it must the Vagabond exhaust to take the Daylight Strike action, and can an exhausted or damaged copy pay that cost?
answer.ruling: Strike exhausts one crossbow to remove one enemy warrior; only when that enemy has no warriors there may it remove another faction piece instead. Actions require a face-up undamaged item, so exhausted or damaged crossbow cannot pay.
